target.title: fix(qa-lab): close transport before gateway teardown
target.body:
Closes #106005

## What Problem This Solves

QA Smoke scenarios can finish successfully while Crabline transport work is still delivering an HTTP response. The suite stopped the gateway first, so that in-flight delivery became an unhandled `HTTP response closed before delivery completed` rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Close the transport before stopping the gateway. Transport cleanup drains outstanding provider HTTP work while the gateway can still accept delivery. The cleanup-order regression test preserves that ordering even when cleanup reports an error.

## User Impact

QA Smoke no longer reports a post-success unhandled rejection caused by its own teardown order. Runtime behavior outside QA Lab is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact-head focused QA extension suite on `fd41dc3f1c600cd948e37f97a2078122ebde868b`: 29 passed.
- Exact-head QA smoke on the QA Lab gateway plus `qa-channel` transport: `channel-chat-baseline` passed 1/1; the captured output reached `CRABBOX_PHASE:complete` and explicitly confirmed `TEARDOWN_REJECTION:absent`.
- Remote proof ran from a fresh detached checkout using DigitalOcean Crabbox (`provider=digitalocean`, lease `cbx_ff0b1c157c92`, public networking, Tailscale disabled); the lease was deleted after validation.
- Formatting and type-aware OXLint passed for the two changed files.
- Fresh autoreview found no in-scope actionable findings.
- Current main's `d9623bd46f` owns the previously failing Crabline fixture/type-contract update; this PR intentionally contains only teardown ordering and its regression test.

## Limitations

The full extension test-type project was not green locally because current main had unrelated iMessage nullability errors during the initial repair. The exact-head remote proof above covers this PR's changed behavior.
